challenges.title: Optimize Array Sum
challenges.description: This code finds the sum of all elements, but it's unnecessarily complex. Simplify it!
hints: The inner loop only runs once - it's useless!
Consider using array methods like reduce()
You can sum an array in a single line with reduce

challenges.title: Simplify Conditions
challenges.description: This function checks grades but has redundant conditions. Clean it up!
hints: Once you check score >= 90, you know score < 90 in the else branch
You don't need to check both ends of the range
Handle edge cases (invalid scores) first

challenges.title: Faster Lookup
challenges.description: This code checks if items exist in a list but gets slower as the list grows. Optimize it!
hints: Nested loops give O(n*m) complexity
Set has O(1) lookup instead of O(n)
Convert one array to a Set, then filter the other

challenges.title: Efficient String Building
challenges.description: This function builds a string inefficiently. Find a better way!
hints: JavaScript has a built-in string method for this
String.prototype.repeat() does exactly this
One line solution is possible!

challenges.title: Flatten Callback Hell
challenges.description: This code has deeply nested callbacks. Refactor with modern async/await!
hints: Wrap callback functions in Promises
Use async/await for sequential async operations
Error handling can use try/catch instead of callbacks
improvements: Use async/await for flat, readable code

challenges.title: Remove Duplicates
challenges.description: This code removes duplicates but is O(n²). Make it faster!
hints: Sets have O(1) lookup
dict.fromkeys() preserves order in Python 3.7+
You can also use list(set(arr)) if order doesn't matter
improvements: Use dict.fromkeys() for O(n) with order preserved

challenges.title: Single Pass Processing
challenges.description: This code iterates multiple times when once would suffice. Optimize it!
hints: Each map/filter/reduce creates a new array and iterates
Combine all operations into a single reduce
Process, filter, and accumulate in one pass

challenges.title: Remove Redundancy
challenges.description: This code has unnecessary variables and steps. Clean it up!
hints: The comparison n % 2 == 0 already returns True or False
You don't need an if/else to return a boolean
Just return the comparison directly!
